inverted_tagged_mono1.note: Pixels inverted and PhotometricInterpretation = MONOCHROME1 (header is honest; the fix is to honor the tag)

inverted_tag_wrong.note: Pixels inverted but tagged MONOCHROME2 (header lies; only looking at the image reveals it)

flipped_left_right.note: Image mirrored left-right (burned-in markers read backwards). Laterality is unsafe: exclude, do not repair

low_resolution_512.note: Matrix 512x512 instead of 1024x1024 (protocol requires 1024); pixel spacing doubled consistently

corrupt_truncated.note: File truncated partway through the pixel data; cannot be decoded

burned_in_phi.note: Synthetic patient name, MRN and birth date drawn into the top-left corner of the pixels (SYNTHETIC; not real people)

patient_id_variants.note: PatientID upper-cased (4), with a leading space (4), or with a SITE1- prefix (4); same patient would not match across files

sex_variants.note: PatientSex written MALE/FEMALE (5), blank (5), or lower case (5) instead of M/F

age_problems.note: Age as 062Y (20; standard DICOM format, harmless; the other 220 files use bare numbers like 62), blank (8), implausible 212Y/150Y (2)

view_position_blank.note: ViewPosition blank, but SeriesDescription still says 'view: PA/AP' (recoverable from another field)

phi_in_header.note: Synthetic patient name, birth date and MRN in header tags (SYNTHETIC; not real people)

modality_dx.note: Modality DX where the rest of the set says CR (both can describe a chest radiograph; the mix is an inconsistency to normalize)

exact_duplicate.note: Byte-identical copy of another file under a different name (same SOPInstanceUID)

same_pixels_new_ids.note: Same pixels submitted again under new SOP/Study/Series UIDs and a new PatientID. In 2 of the 4 the labels file gives the OPPOSITE label to the original

followup_same_patient.note: Different image (shifted, noise added), same PatientID, later StudyDate, same label: a second study of the same patient. A random image-level split would leak patients across train/test

non_chest_image.note: Three images that are not chest radiographs (blank noise, gradient, checkerboard) but whose headers say CHEST; no label, no score

label_spelling_variants.note: Label written PTX/pneumothorax/'Pneumothorax ' (9) or 'no pneumothorax'/Normal/'NO PNEUMOTHORAX' (9) instead of the two standard strings

label_conflict.note: For 2 of the 'same_pixels_new_ids' copies, labels.csv gives the opposite label to the original file

label_without_image.note: labels.csv rows for images that are not in images/

scores_as_logits.note: 25 rows have all four scores as logits (can be negative or above 1) while the rest are probabilities in [0,1]

scores_missing_row.note: Image has a label but no row in model_scores.csv

scores_key_case.note: image_file written in upper case (IMG_0012.DCM): a case-sensitive join misses them

decoys_not_errors: lossy JPEG compression (JPEG baseline transfer syntax) on untouched files
bare-number PatientAge (e.g. '62') in most files (real quirk of the source data)
burned-in 'AP', 'PORTABLE', and L/R markers in real images (not PHI; possible shortcut features)
visible chest tubes / drains in many pneumothorax images (possible shortcut feature for a classifier)
a few real images are rotated, shifted or have black margins (the source data is heterogeneous; not planted)
pediatric patients (age under 18) in the sample: not an error, but excluded by the protocol
